Summary: The Russian Federation reiterated its concern regarding the EU delay in updating technical information in the TRACES-NT system on Russian fish enterprises approved for exports, which hindered exports of Russian fish and animal products to the EU market. The Russian Federation indicated that the European Union was not renewing information and blocking the correction of errors. The Russian Federation was of the view that the delays in the renewal of authorizations constituted a discriminatory trade restriction. Referring to Article 5 of the SPS Agreement, the Russian Federation urged the European Union to base its SPS measures on a risk assessment, based on international standards, guidelines, and recommendations, and not to hinder trade through technical restrictions. In the absence of a response from the European Union in the Committee meeting, the Russian Federation took the floor again to state that the lack of substantive answer showed a low level of transparency and diminished the authenticity of EU statements that the sanctions imposed on the Russian Federation and other measures did not cover agriculture products and foodstuffs.

StatementSubmitted: The European Union is raising a new concern regarding the countrywide import bans that Colombia maintains on pork and pork products from some EU Member States that have reported outbreaks of African swine fever in the past or currently; and on poultry genetic material of some EU Member States that have reported outbreaks of Highly pathogenic Avian Influenza in the past or currently.The EU has requested Colombia several times in meetings, most recently in a meeting with the Colombian competent authorities held in Bogota on 28 May, to apply both the regionalisation concept to pork and poultry products imported from the EU and accept WOAH self-declarations of freedom from ASF, as in the case of Belgium, which is free from ASF since December 2020. Unfortunately, no progress has been made until now.The disease-free areas are established according to WOAH standards in the EU Members States and the competent authority in the exporting EU Member State is responsible for issuing export certificates only for products originating from these areas. The EU reminds Colombia of its obligation to accept pork safe commodities which have been treated in line with the methods foreseen in Article 15.1.23 of WOAH terrestrial code. The EU requests again Colombia to comply with its obligations, in accordance with the WTO SPS Agreement and the relevant WOAH standards and allow trade from disease free areas.
Summary: The European Union expressed concerns regarding country-wide import bans maintained on pork and pork products from some EU member States that had reported outbreaks of African swine fever (ASF), and on poultry genetic material of some EU member States that had reported outbreaks of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI). The European Union had, on several occasions, requested Colombia to apply the regionalization concept to pork and poultry products and accept WOAH self-declarations of freedom from ASF. The European Union recalled that disease-free areas were established according to WOAH standards and that national competent authorities were responsible for issuing export certificates only for products from these areas. The European Union requested Colombia to comply with its obligations, in accordance with the SPS Agreement and WOAH standards, and allow trade from disease-free areas.

StatementSubmitted: Costa Rica plantea su preocupación en relación con las demoras indebidas que está aplicando República Dominicana en el proceso para la habilitación de Costa Rica para la exportación de productos de origen animal como carne de res, carne de cerdo, carne de pollo, embutidos y productos lácteos. Desde marzo del 2022, la Dirección General de Ganadería (DIGEGA) ha descontinuado dicho proceso. La justificación de República Dominicana ha sido que el atraso se debe a cambios en el personal.Entre los meses de febrero y marzo del 2022, la DIGEGA realizó una nueva evaluación a Costa Rica, la cual incluyó una visita in situ. Sin embargo, a la fecha Costa Rica no ha recibido el informe y, por lo tanto, no cuenta con los requisitos sanitarios ni con la habilitación.Por el contrario, ese mismo año, el Ministerio de Salud de República Dominicana realizó una visita in situ a los establecimientos y posteriormente, sin demoras indebidas, emitió la aprobación de éstos.Después de numerosas comunicaciones, fue hasta setiembre del 2023 que la DIGEGA informó oficialmente que aún no ha finalizado el proceso. La DIGEGA manifestó que después de la visita de inicios del 2022 hubo cambios de personal, razón por la cual quedó inconcluso el proceso de elaboración y entrega de los informes y la homologación de los requisitos sanitarios, motivo por el cual Costa Rica no aparece en el listado de países habilitados que maneja el nuevo personal y no puede exportar.Han pasado más de 2 años desde la visita de inspección, y de los cambios en el personal que manifestó la DIGEGA como justificación del atraso; sin embargo, aún no se ha obtenido una respuesta.Costa Rica considera como injustificadas e incongruentes las razones presentadas por República Dominicana para no continuar con el proceso de habilitación. Costa Rica recuerda que el párrafo 1.a) del Anexo C del Acuerdo MSF, señala que los procedimientos que se inicien para verificar el cumplimiento de una medida sanitaria deben ser finalizados sin demoras indebidas, lo que no ha sido cumplido por República Dominicana.Por lo antes expuesto, Costa Rica solicita a las autoridades de República Dominicana retomar y finalizar sin más demoras indebidas el proceso para la habilitación sanitaria de Costa Rica en productos de origen animal.Finalmente, agradecemos el diálogo que tuvimos hoy en una reunión bilateral y esperamos poder resolver la preocupación con prontitud.
Summary: Costa Rica raised concerns regarding undue delays in the authorization of establishments exporting animal products, such as beef, pork, chicken, and dairy products. The Dominican Republic had discontinued the process for authorization on account of changes in staff. While an assessment had been carried out in early 2022, it was only in 2023 that the Dominican Republic had reported that the process had not been finalized. To Costa Rica, the reason advanced for the delay, namely, a change in staff, was not a proper justification. Costa Rica reminded that, under Annex C to the SPS Agreement, procedures needed to meet certain standards and be finalized without undue delays. Costa Rica requested the Dominican Republic to finalize the process for market access.

China raised concerns relating to Import Alert 99-30 of the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), which had had an important impact on trade. China had taken measure to eliminate the illegal addition of melamine and hoped that the United States had seen the results of China's efforts. China had provided materials for FDA evaluation, including laws, regulations, standards, and management measures that melamine should not be artificially added to dairy products. China requested the United States to lift Import Alert 99-30 and measures on dairy products from China.

StatementSubmitted: Thank you, Chair.Before I begin… allow me to congratulate you on your appointment.My delegation looks forward to working with you.We also wish to extend our appreciation to the outgoing Chair.Chair, Indonesia wishes to raise concerns… regarding import restrictions imposed by Chinese Taipei on food products… due to residues of Ethylene Oxide and Sulphur Dioxide.Chinese Taipei has mandated that Ethylene Oxide and its derivatives… must not be present in food products.However, Ethylene Oxide residue is not regulated under the Codex standards.We also observed that other food products from Indonesia… were reported to contain Sulphur Dioxide… with levels exceeding the threshold limit.Chinese Taipei classifies Sulphur Dioxide as a bleaching agent… not as a preservative… and enforces a stringent limit of 30 ppm… significantly lower than the Codex international standard of 300 ppm.Indonesia requests transparency from Chinese Taipei in accordance with Article 7 of the SPS Agreement… concerning export requirements for processed food products to Chinese Taipei… to ensure compliance with Chinese Taipei FDA standards prior to shipment.Indonesia also asks the Chinese Taipei to elaborate the scientific basis… and necessity of the requirements related to residues in food products.We request the Chinese Taipei… to adjust the regulation pertaining to residue limits… by prioritizing international standards and using a less trade-restrictive approach.Furthermore, Indonesia also seeks clarification… regarding the analytical methods used by Chinese Taipei to detect Ethylene Oxide contamination… and hopes that the analytical testing conducted by Indonesia would be deemed acceptable to Chinese Taipei… as per Article 4 of the SPS Agreement.Thank you, Chair.
Summary: Indonesia raised concerns regarding import restrictions imposed on food products due to residues of Ethylene Oxide and Sulphur Dioxide. Indonesia indicated that Ethylene Oxide residues were not regulated by Codex and that Chinese Taipei classified Sulphur Dioxide as a bleaching agent, which led to the application of a residue limit more stringent than the Codex standard. Indonesia requested Chinese Taipei to be more transparent on its requirements for processed food products in accordance with Article 7 of the SPS Agreement, elaborate on the scientific basis for its residue related requirements, and adjust such requirements prioritizing international standards. Indonesia also sought clarification regarding analytical methods used to detect Ethylene Oxide and hoped its own analytical testing would be acceptable in line with Article 4 of the SPS Agreement.

StatementSubmitted: Thank you, Chair.Indonesia wishes to raise concerns… regarding import restrictions imposed by the Philippines on rabbits from Indonesia.The restrictions started in 2021… upon the finding of Rabbit Haemorrhagic Disease Virus (RHDV)… in rabbits exported from Indonesia… based on serologic tests carried out by the Philippines authority.Following this finding… we carried out tests to identify the existence of RHDV among rabbits to be exported from Indonesia.RHDV tests carried out by Indonesia using the PCR method… indicated negative results… which means the virus is non-existent in those rabbits.The PCR method has a higher level of sensitivity and accuracy… to detect RHDV… compared to serologic method.As such, we hope the Philippines could consider the negative result of PCR tests… conducted by the Indonesian authorities.We also would like to seek clarification from the Philippines… regarding the Philippines’ animal disease status of RHDV.Thank you, Chair.
Summary: Indonesia raised concerns regarding import restrictions on rabbits from Indonesia. These restrictions had been applied as of 2021 following the detection of the rabbit haemorrhagic disease virus (RHDV) in rabbits based on serologic tests carried out by the Philippines. Indonesia had carried out tests using the PCR method, which had indicated negative results. Indonesia noted that the PCR method had a higher level of sensitivity and accuracy to detect RHDV, compared to the serologic method that had been used by the Philippines. Indonesia hoped the Philippines could consider these PCR tests and sought clarification regarding the Philippines' animal disease status for RHDV.

StatementSubmitted: India would like to express its concerns regarding the non-renewal of the approval of the active substance thiacloprid in Tea and lowering its MRLs to a limit of determination (LOD). Since the comments period is open upto 7.7.2024 and India would like to urge EU to consider the comments of all stakeholders before finalzing the measure. India would also like to highlight here that “provisional” lowering of the import tolerance for tea will lead to irreversible damage. Changing MRLs has always a long-term effect. A “provisional” change of MRLs is not realistic because the use of active substances and their resulting residues cannot be adjusted instantaneously. This process requires intricate coordination throughout the entire supply chain, particularly for durable products like tea. India also strongly support that a reasonable period should be allowed before the modified MRLs become applicable in order to permit Member States, third countries and food business operators to prepare themselves to meet the new requirements which will result from the modification of the MRLs. India would also like to highlight that Thiacloprid, is animportant substance currently used in India for plant protection to tackle the Tea Mosquito Bug (TMB). The MRLs for tea corresponded to import tolerances which were confirmed to be safe for consumers by EFSA in 2023. Thereby the MRL for Tea was proposed at 10 mg/ kg while for most of the other commodities it was proposed at the LOD 0.01 mg/kg. The Indian tea industry has been impacted by climate change over the past one decade as the industry have been witnessed a decrease of 200 mm rainfall and increase of 1.3 °C average temperature over the years. Tea pests especially Tea Mosquito Bug cause more damage to the crop through increased reproductive potential, feeding rate, distribution pattern, shorter duration of development stages and consequently with a greater number of annual generations with secondary pest outbreaks. The decision to restrict use of Thiacloprid by the European Parliament in its 17th January 2024 resolution would lead to severe crop loss and severely affect tea exports to Europe as there are no corresponding alternative plant protection measure to tackle Tea Mosquito Bug. The EU’s MRL regulatory policies are more trade restrictive than necessary to achieve the EU’s appropriate level of protection. In view of the foregoing, India requests the European Union to re-consider its Regulation as this measure is more trade restrictive than necessary.
Summary: India expressed concerns regarding the non-renewal of the approval of the active substance thiacloprid in tea and the lowering of its maximum residue limits (MRLs) to a limit of determination (LOD). Noting that the comment period was still running, India urged the European Union to consider comments of all stakeholders. India highlighted that the provisional lowering of the import tolerance for tea would lead to irreversible damage, noting that the use of active substances and resulting residues could not be adjusted instantaneously. In this context, India strongly supported that a reasonable implementation period of time should be provided to prepare for new requirements. India also indicated that thiacloprid was an important substance for plant protection to tackle the tea mosquito bug. The EU decision to restrict use of thiacloprid would lead to severe crop loss and severely affect tea exports to Europe as there was no corresponding alternative plant protection measure to tackle the tea mosquito bug. India requested the European Union to reconsider its measure as it was more trade-restrictive than necessary.

StatementSubmitted: India would like to express its concerns regarding the delay in the approval and listing of Indian establishments seeking to export dairy products to Russia, as managed by the Federal Service for Veterinary and Phytosanitary Surveillance (FSVPS). In 2014, two Indian establishments were approved by FSVPS after a physical inspection, yet they remained unlisted on the official website until April 2023. Additionally, seven dairy product establishments applied for listing with FSVPS in 2024, but only one has been listed, and that establishment has been subjected to further special requirements for exports. For the remaining six establishments, FSVPS has insisted on conducting physical inspections without any scientific justification, creating unnecessary trade barriers.All these establishments have been certified by India's official certification body, the Export Inspection Council (EIC), which is also recognized by FSVPS for Indian marine products. EIC adheres to international standards and protocols set by Codex, such as HACCP and FSMS, for certifying establishments for exports.India requests that Russia expedite the listing of these Indian establishments. Furthermore, India urges Russia to withhold from requiring physical inspections for establishments certified by EIC, as this would minimize redundancy in procedures and inspections, reducing costs and delays in dairy exports from India to Russia.

India would like to express its concerns regarding the delays in the approval and listing of Indian establishments interested in exporting egg products to Russia by the Federal Service for Veterinary and Phytosanitary Surveillance (FSVPS). Additionally, India is concerned about the duplication of procedures and inspections, which has led to increased costs and delays in exporting egg products to Russia.To date, Russia has approved and listed only four egg product establishments in India, significantly limiting the ability of Indian businesses to export these products. Requests for additional establishments submitted since September 2022 have been stalled due to the insistence on physical inspections without any scientific justification.India requests that Russia eliminate the requirement for physical inspections for establishments certified by India's official certification body, the Export Inspection Council (EIC), which is also recognized by FSVPS for Indian marine products. Furthermore, India urges Russia to update and publish the lists of Indian products and establishments pending registration or approval and to provide clear timelines for the approval process.

India raises its concerns regarding the EU's Notification No. G/SPS/N/EU/787, dated 12 July 2024, which proposes a revised Maximum Residue Levels (MRLs) for Acetamiprid in certain food commodities, As per the notification, the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) has recommended lowering the existing acetamiprid MRLs for 38 commodities.The Codex MRL of Acetamiprid for tomato and cabbage is 0.2 and 0.7 mg/kg, respectively. However, the EU has lowered the MRLs to 0.06 mg/Kg for tomato and 0.03 mg/Kg for cabbage. Similarly, the proposed revised levels for other commodities like grapes, cucumber, banana and melons have been made very stringent than the Codex levels. This deviation is not based on risk assessment as per provisions of the SPS Agreement. Thus, India urges the EU to reconsider the revised MRLs and adopt the Codex standards on MRLs where available. India also requests the EU, as per Article 5.8 of the SPS Agreement, to provide an explanation for the deviation from applicable international standard.

India seeks to raise concern regarding implementation of UK’s decision to withdraw approval of the active substance mancozeb in Great Britain. The decision relates to placing on the market of mancozeb and plant protection products containing it,  based on the EFSA inclusive study.  The UK’s in its response to India’s comments submitted on G/TBT/N/GBR/70 communicated that a separate action to amend Great Britain’s MRL of mancozeb in various food products would be considered. India urges UK to conduct comprehensive risk assessment on the effects of mancozeb on human health and safety, prior to setting the MRL limits. In this regard, the UK is requested to share the status of review of MRLs for mancozeb and information related to plans to conduct a comprehensive risk -assessment, if any. India also requests the UK to reconsider the decision on non-renewal of active substance mancozeb and consider international standards and other WTO Member practices in this regard. Mancozeb is a common fungicide used world over and its non-renewal and subsequent MRLs have ability to disrupt the agricultural trade and put immense burden on the exports from developing countries. Therefore, India requests the UK to not adopt hazard-based approach while implementing non-tariff measures.

India expresses its concerns regarding the UK's SPS notification no. G/SPS/N/GBR/54, through which Great Britain has set default MRLs of 0.03* mg/kg for imazethapyr on groundnut and rice.As per the Health and Safety Executive (HSE), Great Britain’s evaluation report linked in the notification, “[A]s no specific MRLs are currently established for imazethapyr in the GB MRL Statutory register, HSE recommends that for all other products listed in Part 1 of the register the MRLs are set on the basis of the lowest LOQ validated for plant commodities and at the default LOQ MRL for animal commodities.” Accordingly, the MRL for groundnuts and rice have been set at the LOQ i.e. 0.03 mg/KG. However, it may be noted that Codex MRL for groundnut (peanut) as well as rice is 0.1 mg/Kg. Thus, the UK has deviated from the international standard for MRLs for Imazethapyr for several products, including groundnuts and rice. This deviation is without any scientific justification and is not based on risk assessment as per the provisions of SPS Agreement. India requests the UK, as per Article 5.8 of the SPS Agreement, to provide an explanation for the deviation from applicable international standard.  The UK’s MRL standard for Imazethapyr does not align with Codex Alimentarius levels. We urge the UK to harmonize its standards with Codex to prevent trade barriers in line with WTO’s principles of harmonization.

India would like to express its concerns regarding Hong Kong, China's regulatory limit for Ethylene Oxide (EtO), which is set at the level of quantification (LOQ) i.e. 0.01 mg/Kg which is drastically lower than the limits set by other WTO Members. There is no international standard for Maximum Level (ML) of EtO in food products, including spices and WTO Member practices vary.It may be noted that Hong Kong had conveyed the following in its statement to the Codex Committee on Contaminants in Food (CCCF) in response to Circular Letter 2022/84-CF1 dated December 2022: “Hong Kong does not have a MRL for EtO nor is it an exempted pesticide under the Regulation. CFS considers that it cannot be shown by risk assessment that the consumption of food contaminated by EO is not dangerous or prejudicial to health.”Thus, Hong Kong, China’s regulatory limit for EtO at LOQ for spices is not based on proper risk assessment and is without any scientific reason. The said measure is adopted on precautionary or hazard basis. Therefore, this SPS measure is against Articles 2.2, 5.1, 5.6 and 5.7 of the SPS Agreement.  Furthermore, Ethylene is generated naturally by spices and can covert to EtO. This has not been accounted for by Hong Kong, China’s while adopting and implementing residue limit for EtO in spices.In this context, fixing of ETO regulatory limit at the LOQ level by Hong Kong, China’s is trade restrictive and has resulted in rejection of spice consignments exported to Hong Kong from India. Further, the regulatory limit for ETO is fixed by Hong Kong, China’s on a hazard basis and lacks sufficient risk assessment and scientific basis and the same should be re-considered. India seeks further clarity on why Hong Kong, China’s prefers hazard-based approach over risk-based assessments which factors in real-world conditions.

India expresses its concern regarding the SPS Notification No. G/SPS/N/FRA/20, dated 06 March 2024, issued by France. This notification suspends the entry and import into France of fresh fruits and vegetables from that have been treated with a plant protection product containing Thiacloprid.  The French measure is applicable to all fresh fruits and vegetables and does not take into account the distinctions among various food products and their respective MRL limits.  It may also be noted that Codex MRL for Thiacloprid are in place for several fresh fruits and vegetables. The concerned measure deviates from the international standards without any scientific justification in accordance with the SPS Agreement. Furthermore, the notification states that measure is “precautionary” in nature. Therefore, it cannot be considered in compliance with the Article 5.7 of the SPS Agreement which allows for provisional measures under certain conditions. Thus, India urges France to withdraw its measure and adhere to the available international standards. India also requests the France to provide explanation for deviation from international standards in accordance with Article 5.8 of the SPS Agreement.

Over the last months, China has imposed import restrictions on EU animal products from several EU Member States in relation to the Blue Tongue disease. The EU would like to thank China for the replied received today to a letter sent by the EU on 14 October 2024. In its reply, China indicates that the bluetongue outbreak in EU member countries carries a high risk to China’s animal health and animal husbandry industry, and that on this basis China has decided to suspend the import of cattle and related products from those EU countries suffering the epidemic.The EU would like to recall the provisions of the Terrestrial Code from the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), to which China is a member. Regarding the Blue Tongue disease, Article 8.3.2 of the WOAH Code specifies the safe commodities for which no import restrictions should be imposed, regardless of the blue tongue status of the exporting country.The import restrictions imposed by China on imports of animal products due to the Blue Tongue disease therefore go against international trade rules and standards. The EU would therefore ask China to lift the import restrictions imposed on several EU Member States in relation to the Blue Tongue disease.

Chile presenta ante este comité, su preocupación por las demoras indebidas en el proceso de autorización fitosanitaria para el ingreso al mercado sudafricano de kiwis frescos chilenos.En marzo de 2021, Chile remitió la información técnica solicitada por la ONPF de Sudáfrica para la importación de kiwi fresco, sin contar hasta la fecha con una respuesta respecto al estado de revisión de dichos antecedentes. Esta demora prolongada afecta a los productores y exportadores de kiwis en Chile, quienes, pese al reconocimiento global de la calidad y seguridad fitosanitaria de sus productos, ven limitada, sin justificación alguna, la oportunidad de acceder a este mercado y expandir sus destinos de exportación.Según el Anexo C del Acuerdo MSF, los procedimientos de control, inspección y aprobación deben completarse sin demoras indebidas, lo que claramente no se ha cumplido en este caso, transcurriendo más de tres años sin que la autoridad fitosanitaria de Sudáfrica informe acerca del avance de la revisión de los antecedentes remitidos por Chile a comienzos de 2021. Por otra parte, Sudáfrica no ha informado las etapas del proceso de autorización ni los plazos normales de tramitación involucrados, pese a las reiteradas solicitudes de Chile por las distintas vías bilaterales.Dado que Chile ha entregado de manera oportuna la información requerida para el inicio del Análisis de Riesgo de Plagas (ARP) por parte de Sudáfrica, solicitamos a Sudáfrica la conclusión del ARP para concretar el establecimiento de los requisitos fitosanitarios necesarios para que se concreten las exportaciones de kiwi chileno.En base a lo señalado, Chile insta respetuosamente a Sudáfrica a establecer un canal de comunicación e intercambio de comunicación abierto, con un cronograma de trabajo claro y transparente, que permita una evaluación de los riesgos expedita y sin generar obstáculos innecesarios al comercio. Finalmente, la Delegación de Chile reafirma su disposición a mantener un diálogo abierto y cordial en esta materia con Sudáfrica, y agradece desde ya, la atención a esta preocupación, reiterando la importancia de asegurar una resolución expedita lo más pronto posible.

The European Union regrets to note the countrywide import bans imposed by Thailand on pork and pork products from EU Member States that have reported outbreaks of African swine fever in the past or currently. Thailand has issued several WTO notifications extending these bans.The EU has raised this matter bilaterally with Thailand at many  occasions during meetings. It has also provided comments (including questions) on repeated Thai SPS WTO notifications banning certain Member States. Unfortunately, no progress has been made until now. The EU comments, contrary to recommended practices, have never been answered.The disease-free areas are established according to WOAH standards in the EU Member States. The competent authority in the exporting EU Member State is responsible for issuing export certificates only for products originating from these disease-free areas. Many trading partners in this room recognize the EU regionalization system to date and trade with EU disease free areas, with an excellent safety record.ASF is a global threat and it would be mutually beneficial to secure progress on recognition of regionalization, always with in full respect of applicable international standards.The EU reminds Thailand of its obligation to accept pork safe commodities which have been treated in line with the methods foreseen in Article 15.1.23 of WOAH terrestrial code.The EU calls on Thailand to engage constructively with the EU in order to lift this barrier, allowing trade from disease free areas, in accordance with the WTO SPS Agreement and the relevant WOAH standards.

The European Union would like to raise a new Specific Trade Concern related to the United States overly complex, burdensome, and lengthy approval procedures for imports of plants and plant products from the EU. Despite continuous exchanges at technical level, very little progress has been made over the last years to the EU market access requests. In the last ten years, the U.S. granted only three new market access authorisations from EU Member States. Recently, the US recognised the country freedom for 21 Member States for  two plant pests (ALC and CLB), and published the initial notice for two applications relating to the export of Orchids.This is a much welcome development but a small advance if we look at the more than 30 pending market access applications. Most of the EU’s applications were submitted more than a decade ago, several of the applications even more than 2 decades ago.More than 1/3 of the EU applications are currently at the administrative stage of drafting the initial notice, meaning that all technical work has been finalised already some time ago. The EU is concerned that this is becoming an important bottleneck in the procedure as some applications have been at this stage of drafting the notice for nearly three years with no advances.Unfortunately, during our regular bilateral dialogues the US has not provided any indicative timelines nor indicated when the pending applications are likely to be concluded. Today 20 steps are needed in the US application procedure of which only the first 6 steps are scientific steps. The EU strongly believes that a simplification of the procedure would be to the mutual benefit, without undermining the level of plant health protection. This would result in making the best use of the scarce resources on both sides. The EU calls upon the United States to honor its obligations under the WTO SPS Agreement, to base its import approval procedure on science, to simplify its import approval procedure to avoid undue delays and allow expeditious imports of plants and their products from the EU.

Since 2021, Brazil has been exporting beef to Thailand without any major importing issues. In August 2024, Thailand carried out an inspection mission to Brazilian slaughterhouses, as part of a routine review. As expected, the mission did not indicate any relevant non-conformities.Despite having met all the requirements agreed with the Thai authorities, Brazil was surprised with the decision to suspend imports of beef from our country, right after this inspection mission.After contacting the Thai authorities, Brazil has been informed that Thailand would now require individualtraceability for each animal. However, this requirement is not outlined in any regulation and was not communicated before the mission. Besides, this is a requirement which is not required from other exporters.In all inspection missions, it is general practice to have an initial and a final meeting, during which sanitary authorities highlight any potential issues detected. No traceability concerns were raised at either the opening or the closing meeting. Additionally, Brazil provided Thai authorities with a complete set of translated regulations back to 2019, and no issues were identified at that time.The SPS Agreement stipulates that measures must be proportionate to the risk, transparent, and science based, in reference to Articles 2, 5, and 7. Thailand`s recent decision is surprising because, aside from lacking transparency and prior notification, it imposes more restrictive measures than necessary, despite contrary evidence.Moreover, we believe that Thailand´s suspension of Brazilian exports is inconsistent with the SPS Agreement since it is discriminatory, as it treats trading partners with the same sanitary status differently. This goes against the non-discrimination principle central to the WTO and embedded in Article 2.3 of the SPS Agreement, which outlines the basic rights and obligations of members. Given the seriousness of this issue, Brazil has reached out to the Thai sanitary authorities. We still await a response that addresses our concerns.Therefore, Brazil respectfully requests that the Thai delegation answer the following questions:What Thai regulation requires individual traceability of animals for exports?Does Thailand apply this traceability requirement equally to all trading partners with sanitary statuses comparable to Brazil`s?In light of these points, the Brazilian delegation respectfully asks Thailand to adhere to the clauses of the SPS Agreement and resume imports of Brazilian beef.

The Russian Federation would like to raise the concern regarding delays in Korea's approval procedures for animal products.Previously, Korea informed us | that the issue of beef exports from Russia to Korea will be considered only after Russia re-establishes the official status of WOAH on foot-and-mouth disease as a territory recognized as free from FMD without vaccination.The Russian competent authority has repeatedly informed Korea that currently the Russian Federation has WOAH status as a country with zones recognized as free from FMD with and without vaccination. In May 2022 WOAH admitted Russia as a country which has a controlled BSE risk status. In 2019, Russia provided the Korean side with the data on the regions that are free from FMD without vaccination. Those are the regions from which the exports of beef are planned.In March 2022, the Federal S for V and PH Supervision directed to the Korean side its answers to the questions regarding the risk assessment of beef imports from Bryansk region, Saint-Petersburg and Moscow region.However, no response has been received so far.The Russian Federation urges Korea to comply with its WTO obligations under Articles 6 and 8, and Annex C of the SPS Agreement, so that the approval procedures for Russian animal products are undertaken and completed without undue delay.
